newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAB SLAMS PROPOSED S.AFRICAN LIQUOR BILL.
newsitem.headline: SAB SLAMS PROPOSED S.AFRICAN LIQUOR BILL.

text.p: Brewing giant South African Breweries Ltd on Tuesday rejected as "inappropriate and impractical" certain key aspects of the country's draft liquor bill which aims to restructure the entire industry.

Norman Adami, managing director of SAB's beer division slammed the proposed splitting of the producer-wholesaler link which the bill -- tabled last week and expected to move to parliament in September -- proposes.

"It is inappropriate because, like the rest of the world, SAB believes that all fast moving consumer goods companies are entitled to distribute their products in a manner they believe to be optimum in order to ensure efficiency and effectiveness," Adami said.
He said that SAB, the world's fourth biggest beer brewer, believed that wholesale distribution was a legitimate and integral part of any suppliers' or manufacturers' value chain.
Under the new bill a liquor operation may register only as one type of business. The options are manufacturer, wholesaler, retailer or special events business.
"A person holding an interest in any one type of registration may not acquire interests in any of the other types of registrations," the bill states.
It says that the liquor industry needs to be restructured in order to provide economic empowerment, create sustainable jobs and promote small business development and competition.
But Adami said that it would not result in the intended empowerment of previously disadvantaged communities at wholesaler level.
"The consequences of the draft bill in its present form will not match its intentions," he said.
Business Day newspaper said on Tuesday that the bill could force SAB to divest a 30 percent stake in wine and spirits wholesalers Stellenbosch Farmers Winery Ltd (SFW).
Similarly the tobacco to liquor firm Rembrandt Group Ltd and wine co-operative KWV may have to sell their combined 60 percent stake in SFW and Distillers Corp (South Africa) Ltd .
